standard_prerequisites.name: Closed subsystem
standard_prerequisites.statement: A = <A> means that A is generated by itself, so A is an elementary subsystem of M.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closure of a single element
standard_prerequisites.statement: cl_<(a) = {a} means that the ordering never generates a below itself, which makes a the bottom element above the subsystem.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first of the three conditions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Saturated elementary extension
standard_prerequisites.statement: An omega-saturated extension carries realisations of the types that are consistent over the model.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is where the binary tree of the third condition is realised.

core_obligations: Prove the cycle 1 to 2, 2 to 1, 1 to 3, 3 to 1, checking in each step that the ordering and the generated subsystem match what the next condition requires (source lines 884-891).
For 2 to 1, take an HF-ordering with initial segment A and the new element last, and use that the element is not generated to place it below everything else (source line 886).
For 1 to 3, pass to an omega-saturated elementary extension and realise the type of the binary tree, using the previous structural proposition for consistency (source line 888).
For 3 to 1, observe that the tree is closed under the ordering and use the tree lemma to move the ordering so that the closure of the element is itself, then transfer back to M (source line 891).

proof_roadmap.step: 1 implies 2, by moving the element to the bottom of an ordering.
2 implies 1, from an ordering with the generated subsystem as initial segment.
The equivalence with the saturation condition, through the tree lemma.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 876-883: for an infinite unconfined system, a generated subsystem A and an element outside it, three conditions are equivalent, namely that the closure of the element is itself for some ordering with A as initial segment, that A is elementary in Aa and Aa is elementary in M, and that in some saturated elementary extension there is a binary tree above the element whose closure is the subsystem. The proof (source lines 884-892) is a four-step cycle in which each step is a different mechanism: moving an element to the bottom of an ordering, reading an ordering off an elementary chain, realising a type in a saturated extension, and using the tree lemma to move the ordering so that the closure of the element becomes the element itself. The statement records the three conditions and the extra consequence, and none of the four mechanisms.
